# VoxCtrl — private, on-device voice dictation and Output Command router
# llms.txt — structured index for AI agent discovery
# https://llmstxt.org/

> VoxCtrl is a voice dictation app and programmable speech gateway for Linux (Wayland and X11),
> with a Windows build in beta. It transcribes speech on your own machine with whisper.cpp,
> Moonshine or NVIDIA Parakeet TDT (or an optional OpenAI-compatible remote speech engine you
> point it at), can clean the text up with the on-device S1-mini model, and delivers it to the
> focused window or to named output targets. It also runs a local MCP server so MCP-capable
> agents can use the microphone and text-to-speech as tools.

## Quick Facts

- Version: 0.8.11 (10 Nov 2026)
- License: MIT
- Platform: Linux (Wayland and X11); Windows 10 21H2+ / Windows 11 in beta
- Built with: Rust, Tauri, Svelte
- Repository: https://github.com/JRufer/VoxCtrl
- Website: https://jrufer.com/voxctrl/
- Downloads: VoxCtrl-linux-x86_64-vulkan.AppImage (glibc 2.35+),
  VoxCtrl-linux-x86_64-vulkan-webgpu.AppImage (glibc 2.38+, also GPU for Moonshine and Parakeet),
  VoxCtrl-windows-x86_64-webgpu.exe; on Arch, the AUR packages voxctrl-bin, voxctrl and voxctrl-git
- MCP server: Unix domain socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/voxctrl-mcp.sock, also reachable as
  /tmp/voxctrl-mcp.sock (Linux); named pipe \\.\pipe\voxctrl-mcp (Windows). JSON-RPC 2.0.
- Config: config.json, targets.toml and bindings.toml in VoxCtrl's config directory

## Key Capabilities

1. **On-device transcription** — whisper.cpp, Moonshine and Parakeet TDT (including the Redux and
   English-only Phonon-2 models), each with its own GPU acceleration switch and a built-in Speed test
2. **Output Commands** — 12 delivery types (inject, clipboard, exec, pipe, socket, file, dbus, http,
   webhook, mcp, speak, chat) plus a spoken command router
3. **Dictation cleanup** — S1-mini (Qwen3-0.6B via llama.cpp) on-device, with a different style per app
4. **Dictation history** — kept in memory only by default; optional encrypted persistence via the desktop keyring
5. **MCP server** — transcribe_voice, speak_text, get_status, set_target, get_recent_transcripts (opt-in)
6. **Global hotkeys** — through the XDG GlobalShortcuts portal, so VoxCtrl never reads your keyboard
7. **Local text-to-speech** — Breeze-TTS-2, VoxCPM2, Pocket-TTS, Piper, Inflect and eSpeak-NG
8. **Overlays** — eight built-in styles that show live text while you speak; each is an editable
   index.html + style.css pair

## MCP Integration

Server name: voxctrl
Protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited

### Tools

| Tool                   | Description                                                                  |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| transcribe_voice       | Opens the mic, records the user, returns the transcript                      |
| speak_text             | Queues text for text-to-speech through the current voice                     |
| get_status             | Returns whether the mic is open and TTS is playing                           |
| set_target             | Chooses which output target the next dictations go to; omit the id to list   |
| get_recent_transcripts | Recent dictations from History; only after the user allows it in History     |

### Claude Desktop config

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "voxctrl": {
      "command": "socat",
      "args": ["STDIO", "UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/voxctrl-mcp.sock"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Configuration Files

### targets.toml (output destinations)

Each [[target]] has id, label, delivery and the fields for that delivery type, plus optional
strip_newlines, skip_history and a [target.processing] block overriding remove_fillers,
spoken_punctuation, auto_format_lists and code_mode.

Example:
```toml
[[target]]
id            = "hermes"
label         = "Hermes Agent"
delivery      = "pipe"
pipe_path     = "/tmp/hermes.in"
response_pipe = "/tmp/hermes.out"

[target.processing]
remove_fillers = true
```

### bindings.toml (hotkey gestures)

Each [[binding]] maps keys and a gesture to one or more targets.
Gesture types: hold | toggle | double_tap | double_tap_hold

Example:
```toml
[[binding]]
id        = "default_hold"
label     = "Dictate (Hold)"
keys      = ["KEY_LEFTMETA", "KEY_SPACE"]
gesture   = "hold"
target_id = "default"
```

## Privacy

- No telemetry, no analytics, no automatic crash reporting
- Network requests happen only when you ask: checking for updates (automatic daily checks are off
  unless you turn them on), downloading models or voices, filing a bug report, or targets and
  engines you configure
- Transcripts are not written to the log, only word and character counts
